recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group opens a new issue to standardize concrete contextual-link relations or valid-operation discovery; that would be new scope rather than unfinished FHIR-5883 application.
issue_request: FHIR-5883 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Feed change request raised for DSTU1 asking to support context-dependent links for individual resources and Bundle entries. Final working-group comments narrowed the accepted work to adding Bundle.entry.link, documenting that transaction meaning is implementation specific, and noting its relationship to HTTP Link headers.
initial_application: Commit dc91fb8899aa4b7af62f7b5c69b6f43f6e89be9d (#5883 - add link to Bundle.entry, git-svn build@4576) added Bundle.entry.link to the historical bundle spreadsheet as a 0..* @Bundle.link child and added Bundle notes explaining HATEOAS/additional-context use, HTTP header correspondence for directly read resources, and implementation-specific transaction meaning.
additional_context: Bundle is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. Current source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml defines Bundle.entry.link as a repeatable content reference to Bundle.link and includes the accepted guidance. Current source/bundle/bundle-notes.xml repeats the same narrative note. The related FHIR-5884 proposal to standardize valid-operation contextual links was later Resolved - No Change / Not Persuasive, so FHIR-5883 should not be broadened into standardized rel or authorization semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current source already implements the accepted FHIR-5883 infrastructure and explanatory notes; adding more HTTP header or operation-link guidance would exceed the narrowed decision and conflict with the later no-change disposition of FHIR-5884.

related_jiras.note: Separate valid-operation contextual-link pattern referenced by FHIR-5883; resolved Not Persuasive/No Change, supporting no additional standardized link semantics in this reconciliation.
